_doc: Hybrid enrichment groups (user, 2026-10-05: many passes, grouped by tradition so each agent's share is small; every source read; no silent losses; extract (per group unit, lines per position) then place (one call per page)). material: ayah = segments tied to an ayah of the surah (a tie of up to 3 ayat goes to its first ayah's page; a wider or surah-level tie to the page of the single ayah it cites, else the surah page); a held source of an ayah group with no ayah tie anywhere in the corpus is reached by phrase search (the ayah's three-word sequences); cites: true adds segments that cite the surah's ayat without being tied (excerpts); cites = only such citing segments (reference works); search = hits of script-run searches (recorded, caps printed); meal = the pack's meal files; none = the agent searches itself (antecedents). required: every page hears this voice (a block, the agent's recorded reason, or the script's 'no material on this page'). unit: surah = one unit for the whole surah, never split (one verdict, one voice). odak: what the group's agent is for. not_read: sources no group reads, with the reason (printed by plan). Units are packed to budget_chars of material, balanced, split at page boundaries.

groups.odak: Transmitted tafsir: who said what (Companions, Successors, early authorities), with transmitters; who repeats whom; the well-known direct explanations of each key word; reports graded by the shared core's rule 4.
The Kashshāf line of analytical tafsir: grammar, rhetoric and meaning as Zamakhsharī states them and as Bayḍāwī, Nasafī and Abū Ḥayyān take, correct or dispute them.

The comprehensive analytical tafsirs: Rāzī's questions and kalām, Ālūsī's syntheses, Qurṭubī's legal and lexical points, Ibn ʿAṭiyya, and Māwardī's numbered senses (without choosing). Each one's distinctive points; shared points once, with who repeats whom.
Modern Arabic tafsir: Ibn ʿĀshūr's naẓm, rhetoric and maqāṣid; Sayyid Quṭb's literary reading (al-taṣwīr al-fannī); ʿAbduh where present.
Imāmī and Muʿtazilī voices: Ṭabrisī, Ṭabāṭabāʾī (strong on Qur'an by Qur'an), al-Jishumī: where they differ from the Sunni readings and why.

REQUIRED VOICE (user, 2026-10-05: one of the two traditions the user most wants to hear). Biqāʿī's naẓm: the surah's maqṣūd (purpose) and its munāsaba with the neighbouring surahs (surah page), and for every ayah how it serves the maqṣūd and links to the ayah before and after (ayah pages). Every page of the surah gets Biqāʿī's reading, or a recorded reason in kapsam.jsonl.

REQUIRED VOICE (user, 2026-10-05). The bayānī line: the al-Khūlī school (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ's al-Tafsīr al-bayānī and al-Iʿjāz al-bayānī; two secondary studies of al-Khūlī's method) and Fāḍil al-Sāmarrāʾī (Lamasāt bayāniyya, Asrār al-bayān): a word's sense from its whole Qur'anic usage, why this word, form or order and not its near-synonym, the literary and psychological reading; their findings and their principled objections (e.g. one sense in context against reading several latent senses).
Allusive (ishārī) readings: what each adds, marked as allusion, never as the ayah's outward sense.
The maʿānī and gharīb works and grammar: early lexical glosses, syntax that decides meaning, majāz; they are also the first place antecedents of the commentary's images are found.
Readings: canonical, non-canonical and Companion readings, and what each does to meaning; leave out what changes only pronunciation.
The wujūh wa-naẓāʾir books: the senses each lists for the ayah's content words and the ayat it files under each sense.
Turkish tafsir (Elmalılı, Kur'an Yolu): their reading of the ayah and where it differs from the classical and from the commentary.

Occasions of revelation (every competing report with its transmitter and grade), Makkī/Madanī and chronology (kept apart from occasions), ʿulūm al-Qurʾān points, modern reference (TDVİA, Corpus Coranicum).
Sahih hadith only: a direct Prophetic explanation of the ayah's words when one exists, then each hadith that bears on the ayah's words or subject; never a non-sahih report as hadis.

The meal review (zengin.md Step 5) for every ayah of the surah: word-by-word for each ayah page, the losses shared across the surah and the one surah verdict on the surah page; translators judged by patterns across a term's occurrences (corpus.py get MEAL-X:S:A).

Antecedents and counter-evidence for the commentary's own claims that no source line touched (the placement calls' bos.jsonl): search the maʿānī/gharīb works, the wujūh books, Kashshāf, the ishārī works and the full tafsir texts at the word's other occurrences (not the lexica: the base was written from them); then counter-evidence. An oncul line when an antecedent exists, else one yenilik line; record what was searched (taranan, tarama).

Modern commentaries in English (added 2026-10-05): The Study Quran's per-verse synthesis of classical exegesis (its sigla name the commentators) and Asad's reformist notes; what they add to or contest in the page's reading. Skip the Study Quran's translation copy (duplicate).

Coherence (naẓm) of the Farāhī–Iṣlāḥī school: the surah's central theme (ʿamūd), its relation to the paired surah, the section the ayah sits in; Cuypers's rhetorical analysis (parallel and concentric composition) where it treats the passage. Complements nazm-bikai.

Academic reference works reached through the ayat they cite (`corpus.py cites S:A`) and the ayah's key terms (Sinai, Jeffery, Zammit by headword): chronology, loanword and Semitic cognate claims, term histories; reported as positions with their authors, never as the page's own conclusions.

Iʿjāz and balāgha theory (al-Jurjānī's naẓm, al-Bāqillānī, al-Rummānī) where it discusses this ayah or the construction the page's prose turns on (taqdīm, ḥadhf, kināya, istiʿāra…); found by script-run searches of the ayah's phrases and constructions.
Pre- and early-Islamic poetry as shawāhid for the ayah's words: the verses in which a word of the ayah occurs, with the commentator's gloss; found by script-run searches of the content words.
Sīra and akhbār (Ibn Hishām, al-Azraqī's Mecca, Ibn al-Kalbī's idols) where they bear on the ayah's occasion, places, persons or cults; found by searches of the ayah and the names it involves.

Turkish dictionaries for the page's Turkish wording (PACK turkish.md: Nişanyan, TDK, Kubbealtı): the senses and history of the Arabic loanwords the meals and the prose use, and what they have drifted from (anlam_tarihi).

not_read.reason: user, 2026-10-05: «i do not want dictionary since i already have it in my original analysis» — the base was written from the project dictionary (PROJE) and the lexica; no group reads them again, and oncul does not search them for antecedents
